points: Yirmiyahu watches a potter reshape spoiled clay into something new. If the people change, Hashem can remake them. That's the source of "Ki hinei kachomer b'yad hayotzer" on Yom Kippur.
Having the chance to change and not taking it is a real problem.

How do we know a real navi, if bad prophecies can be cancelled by teshuvah? The Rambam: good prophecies never change, so a navi is tested by good predictions coming true. The Abarbanel: only by great miracles, like Moshe.
The people of Anasos plot against Yirmiyahu (some say poison, reporting him to the king, false rumors), and he asks Hashem not to accept their teshuvah.
Like Moshe with Korach: Hashem accepts teshuvah for personal sins, but causing others to sin is a line too far. His own townspeople ignoring him led everyone else to ignore him.
